title: Latency stitchboard: model-route mode comparator (stream vs sync)
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Create a consolidated latency "stitchboard" that lets SREs and product engineers compare p50/p95/p99 across model families and route definitions with a clear split between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. This ticket covers schema decisions, tracing hook instrumentation, metrics/log pipeline updates, visualization design, and rollout to the production dashboard. The goal is to reduce time-to-root-cause for latency regressions that differ by IO mode and model variant.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model families and routes with explicit streaming vs non-streaming panes.
- Percentile computations sourced from both trace-derived latencies and aggregated metric buckets; reconcile differences with a notes panel.
- Trace links for sampled slow requests available from each percentile cell.
- New metrics follow naming conventions and appear in Prometheus and BigQuery pipelines.
- Post-rollout synthetic test verifies parity for <1% deviation versus baseline metrics.
implementation_notes:
Instrumentation: add tracing-hooks to the request router to tag requests with route_id, model_family, io_mode (stream|sync), sequence_length_bucket. Metrics: emit histogram buckets for per-request end-to-end latency and a separate histogram for token-emit latency on streaming requests. Pipeline: update metrics ingestion to compute p50/p95/p99 per (model_family, route_id, io_mode) window and write to the long-term metrics store. Dashboard: Grafana board with split panels — left column non-streaming, right column streaming; include toggle to overlay percentiles and a small table with trace links and error rates.
Trade-offs: maintaining separate histograms increases cardinality; mitigate by bucketing sequence_length and dropping low-cardinality tags on high-cardinality models. We avoided computing percentiles from raw span logs to reduce query cost; instead reconcile with sample traces for validation.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for trace hook tag attachment and histogram emission.
- Integration in staging: run synthetic workload generating streaming and non-streaming traces across two model families; validate percentile outputs.
- End-to-end test: create a canary dashboard panel and compare with baseline metrics for 24h under controlled load.
- Post-deploy: run a regression job that compares produced percentiles to pre-deploy crawl and alerts if drift > 1%.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge instrumentation PR to staging; 2) Enable metrics pipeline consumers in staging; 3) Flip feature flag for dashboard to 'canary' for internal SRE; 4) Monitor for two 12-hour windows; 5) Gradual rollout to production with gate at traffic 25%/50%/100%. If p95 delta > 5% or error rate increases, rollback and open postmortem.
